steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The League of Nations was created as part of the Treaty of Versailles in June 1919. It was Woodrow Wilson's idea - his Fourteenth Point called for "a general association of nations." The League's headquarters were in Geneva, Switzerland. Its first meeting was held on 15 November 1920 with 42 member states.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The League's Covenant (its founding document) set out its key principles: collective security, arbitration of disputes, disarmament, and improved living and working conditions worldwide. Article 10 of the Covenant committed all members to "respect and preserve" each other's territorial integrity.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Council was the most powerful body. It had permanent members (Britain, France, Italy, Japan) who could veto decisions. However, ALL Council decisions had to be UNANIMOUS - any member could veto action. This meant the League was often paralysed by disagreement. A single "no" vote could prevent the League from acting against an aggressor.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The League's membership was fundamentally flawed from the start. The USA never joined; Germany was excluded until 1926; the USSR was excluded until 1934; and Japan and Italy left in the 1930s. No organisation can maintain world peace without the world's most powerful nations.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: The League's THREE WEAPONS (moral condemnation, economic sanctions, military force) are essential to know Always distinguish between 1920s successes and 1930s failures - the League's record is not uniformly bad Aaland Islands (1921) and Greece-Bulgaria (1925) are the best examples of League successes The UNANIMITY RULE is crucial - any member could veto any action, making the League powerless America's absence is the single most important weakness - always include it in your answer The League had NO ARMY - this is fundamental to understanding why it could not stop aggression The humanitarian work (Nansen, ILO, Health Organisation) is often overlooked but important for balanced answers
